options.rationale: signal, check around you, then move; at an intersection begin about three seconds, roughly one hundred feet, before the turn.

options.text: Right as you begin turning
options.rationale: Wrong: signal well before the turn.

options.text: About ten seconds before
options.rationale: Wrong: the guide is about three seconds.

options.text: Only if a car is behind you
options.rationale: Wrong: always signal.

items.correct_rationale: Option A is correct: signal, check around you, then move; at an intersection begin about three seconds, roughly one hundred feet, before the turn.
distractor_source: synthesized near-miss: signal well before the turn.
synthesized near-miss: the guide is about three seconds.
synthesized near-miss: always signal.

items.stem: Your turn is just past an intersection. When do you signal?

options.text: Before entering the intersection
options.rationale: Wrong: that could suggest you are turning at the intersection.

options.text: Never
options.rationale: Wrong: you still signal, after crossing.

options.text: Only after completing the turn
options.rationale: Wrong: you signal after crossing but before turning.

options.text: After you have crossed the intersection
options.rationale: when your turn comes just after an intersection, wait until you have crossed it before signaling.

items.correct_rationale: Option D is correct: when your turn comes just after an intersection, wait until you have crossed it before signaling.
distractor_source: synthesized near-miss: that could suggest you are turning at the intersection.
synthesized near-miss: you still signal, after crossing.
synthesized near-miss: you signal after crossing but before turning.

items.stem: How does signal timing differ for these two turns?

options.text: Both turns are signaled the same way
options.rationale: Wrong: the turn just past an intersection waits.

options.text: Turns just past an intersection are never signaled
options.rationale: Wrong: they are signaled after crossing.

options.text: Signal about three seconds before an intersection turn, but wait until after crossing for a turn just past one
options.rationale: at an intersection you signal about three seconds ahead, but for a turn just past one you wait until you have crossed it.

options.text: Intersection turns are signaled after the turn
options.rationale: Wrong: they are signaled about three seconds before.

items.correct_rationale: Option C is correct: at an intersection you signal about three seconds ahead, but for a turn just past one you wait until you have crossed it.
distractor_source: synthesized near-miss: the turn just past an intersection waits.
synthesized near-miss: they are signaled after crossing.
synthesized near-miss: they are signaled about three seconds before.

items.stem: What do the hand signals mean?

options.text: Arm straight out for right, bent up for left
options.rationale: Wrong: straight out means left and bent up means right.

options.text: Arm straight out for left, elbow bent with hand up for right, hand down to slow or stop
options.rationale: hand signals: straight out for left, bent up for right, pointed down to slow or stop, used when turn signals are missing or hard to see.

options.text: Arm up for stop, down for left
options.rationale: Wrong: down means slow or stop.

options.text: Waving the arm for any turn
options.rationale: Wrong: each signal has a set position.

items.correct_rationale: Option B is correct: hand signals: straight out for left, bent up for right, pointed down to slow or stop, used when turn signals are missing or hard to see.
distractor_source: synthesized near-miss: straight out means left and bent up means right.
synthesized near-miss: down means slow or stop.
synthesized near-miss: each signal has a set position.

items.stem: A driver holds an arm out the window with the elbow bent and hand pointing up. What does it mean?

options.text: A right turn
options.rationale: in hand signals a straight arm means left, an arm bent upward means right, and an arm pointed down means slowing or stopping.

options.text: A left turn
options.rationale: Wrong: a left turn is a straight arm.

options.text: Slowing or stopping
options.rationale: Wrong: that is the arm pointed down.

options.text: Go ahead and pass
options.rationale: Wrong: that is not a hand signal in the handbook.

items.correct_rationale: Option A is correct: in hand signals a straight arm means left, an arm bent upward means right, and an arm pointed down means slowing or stopping.

synthesized near-miss: that is the arm pointed down.
